Generated by scripts/vr-utah-committee-mapping.mjs --seed from db/vr-utah-committee-bills-2024GS.json. Do not hand-edit.

measures.title: Emergency Responder Voting Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses voting procedures for emergency responders.

issues.rationale: Introduced text lets a registered voter who is assisting with an emergency on election day outside the voter's county of residence cast an electronic ballot after filing a declaration of eligibility, and requires the lieutenant governor to report annually. It adds a way for one class of voter to cast a ballot they would otherwise lose, which is a narrow but real access gain.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Dailey-Provost moved to pass H.B. 28 out favorably.

measures.title: Sensitive Material Review Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions regarding the evaluation of instructional material to identify and remove pornographic or indecent material.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires that protecting children from illicit pornography be prioritized over other considerations when instructional material is evaluated, names who may trigger a formal sensitive material review, splits objective from subjective sensitive material, forces statewide removal once a threshold of LEAs finds material objectively sensitive, and orders a compliance audit. Parent-triggered control of classroom material is the whole bill.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hall moved to pass H.B. 29 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McKell moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 29 out favorably.

measures.title: Utah Seismic Safety Commission Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to the Utah Seismic Safety Commission.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text extends the sunset date on the Utah Seismic Safety Commission so the state's standing earthquake preparedness body keeps operating. Keeping preparedness capacity alive is the direction this key measures, and a sunset extension is the narrowest form of it, which is why the weight sits at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Senator Wilson moved to pass H.B. 47 out favorably.

measures.title: Federal Funds Contingency Planning
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses contingency planning related to federal funds.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires a state agency seeking a federal funds reauthorization or a new federal request above a threshold to file a contingency disclosure, a contingency plan, and a state jurisdiction evaluation, and requires agencies above a federal funding threshold to keep a standing contingency plan. The bill exists to prepare the state to operate without federal money, which is the state-autonomy direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Ward moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 59 out favorably.

measures.title: Utah Water Ways Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the partnership of Utah Water Ways.

issues.rationale: First substitute text directs the Utah Water Ways partnership to work with the State Board of Education on standards-aligned conservation resources and professional development, and to promote coordination of grants, rebate programs, and localized conservation messaging, with annual reporting. Conservation outreach is a real but narrow water measure, so it sits at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Bennion moved to pass H.B. 62 out favorably.

measures.title: Gun Safety Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns a waiting period for the sale of a firearm.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates a waiting period between the purchase of a firearm from a dealer and delivery of the firearm to the purchaser, with defined exceptions. A purchase-to-delivery delay is a firearm restriction in the plain sense and is the entire operative content of the bill.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Moss moved to pass H.B. 97 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm Access Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires that a firearm is secured and provides penalties.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires that a firearm be securely stored or rendered inoperable by a locking device and sets civil penalties for violations. A storage mandate backed by penalties is the core of the safe-storage agenda, and the bill does nothing else.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Moss moved to pass H.B. 98 out favorably.

measures.title: Employment Training Requirement Limitations
measures.generalProvisions: This bill prohibits, for purposes of employment discrimination, certain training or other requirements that compel or require adherence to or belief in certain concepts.

issues.rationale: Introduced text makes it employment discrimination for an employer to impose training or other requirements that compel adherence to or belief in specified concepts about race, sex, and related characteristics, while clarifying that objective discussion is still allowed, and adds a severability clause. Banning compelled-belief training is the operative anti-DEI mechanism.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass H.B. 111 out favorably.

measures.title: Olene Walker Housing Loan Fund Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to the Olene Walker Housing Loan Fund within the Department of Workforce Services.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires the Division of Finance to transfer a set amount of state liquor sale revenue from the Liquor Control Fund to the Olene Walker Housing Loan Fund every year. It is a single provision, but it moves ongoing money into the state's affordable housing loan fund rather than studying or reorganizing it.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Briscoe moved to pass H.B. 141 out favorably.

measures.title: Earned Income Tax Credit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill makes the earned income tax credit refundable.

issues.rationale: Introduced text makes the state earned income tax credit refundable, so a low or moderate wage household receives the credit amount that exceeds its liability instead of only zeroing the liability out. Refundability is the whole bill and the benefit lands entirely on working households below the median.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Briscoe moved to pass H.B. 149 out favorably.

measures.title: School Board Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses actions of a school district that may be subject to a referendum.

issues.rationale: First substitute text provides that a law passed by a local school board, other than one imposing a new tax or a tax increase, may be referred to the voters of the school district for approval or rejection, subject to stated exceptions. It creates a ballot route where none existed, which is an access gain, though confined to school district law.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lund moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 161 out favorably.

measures.title: Digital Currency Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill makes modifications to the Uniform Commercial Code.

issues.rationale: Introduced text amends the Uniform Commercial Code so that a central bank digital currency, defined as a digital currency issued by the Federal Reserve System, a federal agency, or a foreign government or central bank, is excluded from money and is not specie. Refusing CBDC legal status as money is the substance of this key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Kwan moved to pass H.B. 164 out favorably.

measures.title: Local School Board Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses actions of a school district that may be subject to a referendum.

issues.rationale: First substitute text provides that a law passed by a local school board that imposes a new tax or increases a tax may be referred to the voters of the school district for approval or rejection. Like its companion, it adds a referendum route that the electorate did not previously have, which is a narrow access gain.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Birkeland moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 173 out favorably.

measures.title: License Plate Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to the issuance of personalized license plates.

issues.rationale: First substitute text defines the words that may appear on a personalized license plate and prohibits the Motor Vehicle Division from issuing a plate whose requested combination is indecent, obscene, profane, or connotes certain illegal activities or substances, with a severability clause. The state is deciding which expressive combinations it will refuse, which is a speech restriction, narrow because the forum is a state-issued plate.

committeeActs.committee: House Transportation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Matthews moved to pass H.B. 186 out favorably.

measures.title: Electrical Energy Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to the regulation of energy.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires the Public Service Commission to act in accordance with the state energy policy, requires stated determinations before it may authorize the early retirement of an electrical generation facility, and requires annual reporting on retirement requests. The operative effect is to make it harder to close existing thermal generation.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Kyle moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 191 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Owens moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 191 out favorably.

measures.title: Clean Energy Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to clean energy.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text replaces renewable with clean throughout the energy statutes, and the clean energy source definition it relies on includes nuclear fuel and carbon capture utilization and sequestration. The qualifying set is broadened past renewables into the all-of-the-above framing this key measures rather than narrowed.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Cobb moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 241 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Water Usage Data Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses water usage data.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires state agencies to report water usage, directs the Division of Water Resources to study public school water use in stated areas and publish findings and recommendations, and provides for procurement of smart irrigation controllers. Measuring and then reducing the state's own water use is a conservation direction, with the controllers giving it operative teeth.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Moss moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 242 out favorably.

measures.title: Initiative Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to a statewide initiative.

issues.rationale: Introduced text, contingent on a constitutional amendment, raises the vote percentage required for a statewide initiative that would impose a new tax or increase a tax rate to pass, and adds application and fiscal impact statement requirements about how a proposed law would be funded. A supermajority threshold means a majority of voters can approve an initiative and still lose, which is a restriction on the ballot route.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Pierucci moved to pass H.B. 284 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Fillmore moved to pass H.B. 284 out favorably.

measures.title: Property Rights Ombudsman Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the Property Rights Ombudsman Act.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text lets a party who prevails in court on an issue the Office of the Property Rights Ombudsman had already decided in that party's favor recover attorney fees, and in stated circumstances collect a civil penalty and consequential damages. It puts money behind a property owner's win against a government entity that ignored the ombudsman.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. King moved to pass H.B. 289 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: School Curriculum Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions that prohibit school officials and employees from endorsing, promoting, or disparaging certain beliefs or viewpoints.

issues.rationale: First substitute text prohibits school officials and employees from using instructional materials or a display of symbols, images, or language to endorse, promote, or disparage a religious belief or a political viewpoint, and has the attorney general defend and the state indemnify those enforcing the prohibition. Whatever the neutrality framing, the operative clause removes expression from public employees in the classroom.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lisonbee moved to pass H.B. 303 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm Data Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns law enforcement data collection and reporting concerning firearms.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires law enforcement agencies to report lost or stolen firearms used in a crime and the disposition of firearms in agency custody, and requires the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice to compile and publish that data. Public firearm data is the evidentiary groundwork of this key, but it regulates no purchase or possession, so it stays at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Elison moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 307 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Driver License Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the information that may be displayed on a driver license or identification card and modifies when the Driver License Division may share information.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text lets a concealed firearm permit holder have the permit number printed on a driver license or identification card, lets that card be presented in place of the permit itself, and sets a five-year expiration for such a license. It removes a document a permit holder must otherwise carry to exercise the permit.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Transportation, Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Riebe moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 309 out favorably.

measures.title: Inmate Assignment Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses inmate housing assignments.

issues.rationale: First substitute text prohibits the Department of Corrections and county jails, with limited exceptions, from assigning inmates of the opposite biological sex to the same housing area. Housing determined by birth sex rather than gender identity is the operative rule, which subtracts from the recognition this key measures.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Birkeland moved to pass H.B. 316 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Motor Vehicle Safety Inspection Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to window tinting.

issues.rationale: First substitute text allows a peace officer to stop a vehicle for improper side window tinting only if the officer has already stopped the vehicle for another offense, and prohibits revoking or suspending a registration or driver license over a tint violation. Removing a stand-alone pretext for a traffic stop is a policing-practice reform.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Clancy moved to pass H.B. 323 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Firearm Safety Incentives
measures.generalProvisions: This bill establishes an income tax credit for the purchase of a firearm safety device.

issues.rationale: Sixth substitute text enacts a nonrefundable individual income tax credit for the purchase of a firearm safety device, limits it to one claim per household, and provides for sunset review. It pays people to lock firearms up, which is the safe-storage direction, but it is an incentive rather than a requirement.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lyman moved to pass 4th Substitute H.B. 326 out favorably.

measures.title: State Grant Process Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts provisions governing the administration of state grants.

issues.rationale: Fourth substitute text requires a state grant recipient to submit a proposed budget and agree to deliverables, reporting, audit, and clawback requirements before receiving any funds, sets the disbursement schedule, requires later review of grants funded by ongoing appropriations, and adds requirements specific to direct award and competitive grants. Every clause attaches accountability to public money.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Michael Petersen moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 335 out favorably.

measures.title: Residential Rental Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill deals with landlords providing notice to tenants.

issues.rationale: Introduced text establishes the period of advance notice a landlord must give a tenant before a rent increase takes effect. It is a single obligation, but it runs entirely in the renter's favor and gives a tenant time to respond to an increase, which is the protection this key measures.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Kwan moved to pass H.B. 355 out favorably.

measures.title: First Responder Mental Health Services Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns mental health services for first responders.

issues.rationale: First substitute text broadens who is eligible for first responder mental health resources, keeps eligibility after a person leaves first responder employment, requires agencies to inform employees of resources and name a liaison, requires the Department of Public Safety to post resource information and investigate denials, and lets the criminal justice commission withhold grants from an agency that improperly denies care. Access to treatment is created and then enforced.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Wilson moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 378 out favorably.

measures.title: Workplace Discrimination Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses religious expression in the workplace.

issues.rationale: First substitute text prohibits an employer from compelling an employee to communicate or act in a manner the employee believes would burden or offend the employee's sincerely held religious beliefs, and sets out a process for accommodating those beliefs. Protecting religious conscience inside employment is the substance of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lisonbee moved to pass H.B. 396 out favorably as amended.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McCay moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 396 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearms Financial Transaction Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses consumer transactions related to firearms.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text prohibits the use of a firearms merchant category code in payment processing, creates a complaint process and civil penalties for violations, and gives the attorney general enforcement power. The bill exists to stop financial intermediaries from flagging lawful firearm purchases, which is a gun-owner protection.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Owens moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 406 out favorably.

measures.title: Presumption of State Jurisdiction Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill affirms state sovereignty and establishes a presumption of state jurisdiction.

issues.rationale: First substitute text declares that jurisdiction over subject matters not enumerated to the federal government remains with Utah, provides that any presumption against state jurisdiction is overcome only by a federal demonstration of specific constitutional authorization, places the burden on the federal government in non-enumerated disputes, and presumes the federal interest in federal lands is proprietary. The bill is a sovereignty claim from top to bottom.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Shipp moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 409 out favorably.

measures.title: Lewdness Involving a Child Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns the offense of lewdness involving a child.

issues.rationale: Fourth substitute text rewrites the elements of lewdness involving a child, reaching simulated masturbation and restating exposure conduct in terms that no longer depend on the actor's gender. The offense covers conduct it did not clearly reach before, which is an expansion of criminal exposure.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lisonbee moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 424 out favorably as amended.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Kennedy moved to pass 4th Substitute H.B. 424 out favorably.

measures.title: Health Insurance Benefit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends and enacts provisions related to health insurance benefits.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires a health benefit plan to ensure pharmaceutical rebates are used for stated purposes, enacts pharmacy network requirements, modifies pharmacy audit rules, and requires a pharmacy benefit manager to offer specified options to self-funded plans. Directing rebate dollars and constraining benefit managers is drug-cost policy aimed at the middlemen.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Wilson moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 425 out favorably.

measures.title: State Employment Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions of the Utah State Personnel Management Act.

issues.rationale: Introduced text classifies a state employee as exempt from career service status beginning January 2025 unless the position requires POST certification, career status is needed to keep federal funding, or the employee held career status before reclassification, and it redefines career service by reference to the system section. Stripping tenure protections from the state workforce is exactly what this key tracks.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Thurston moved to pass H.B. 429 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass H.B. 429 out favorably.

measures.title: Local Government Transportation Services Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill permits public transit innovation grants and amends provisions related to allocation of certain local option sales and use taxes for transportation.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text lets local option sales tax revenue and Transit Transportation Investment Fund money pay for public transit innovation grants, has the Department of Transportation and the Transportation Commission administer and prioritize them, and requires a large transit district to report expenditures, service, and ridership to each municipality. New money for transit service plus accountability for it.

committeeActs.committee: House Transportation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Pulsipher moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 430 out favorably.

measures.title: Blended Plea Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies procedures relating certain convictions of a minor that involve both juvenile dispositions and adult criminal sentences.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text prohibits a court from accepting a plea that blends a juvenile adjudication and disposition with an adult criminal conviction and sentence, and voids any conviction or sentence entered as a prohibited blended plea. It closes a route by which a minor picks up an adult sentence in the same breath as a juvenile disposition.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Loubet moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 459 out favorably.

measures.title: Government Employee Conscience Protection Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses required reasonable accommodations for government employees in certain circumstances.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text requires a governmental entity to grant an employee's request to be relieved from performing a task that violates the employee's conscience, defined as a sincerely held belief about the rightness or wrongness of an action, unless doing so would impose undue hardship, and creates protections and a cause of action for a denied employee. Conscience protection with a remedy attached.

committeeActs.committee: House Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Judkins moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 460 out favorably.

measures.title: Housing Affordability Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses funding issues related to housing affordability.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text authorizes redevelopment and community development agencies to fund acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation of income targeted housing, requires the Department of Workforce Services to create pass-through funding agreements that spend state funds on stated affordable housing investments, modifies the low-income housing tax credit, and adjusts moderate income housing reporting. The bill's money and mandates run toward income-targeted units.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Pierucci moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 465 out favorably.

measures.title: School Transit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates the Transit Access Pass for Students pilot grant program (the program).

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates the Transit Access Pass for Students pilot grant program with application requirements, rulemaking by the state board, reporting, and a sunset date. It puts state grant money behind transit passes for students, which is a service subsidy rather than a study.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Romero moved to pass H.B. 473 out favorably.

measures.title: Technology Upgrade Incentives Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill provides for tax incentives related to certain technology upgrades.

issues.rationale: First substitute text replaces the declining schedule for the alternative fuel heavy duty vehicle tax credit, which was stepping down from fifteen thousand dollars to three thousand, with a flat fifteen thousand dollar credit, and adds a new credit for locomotive idle-reduction devices subject to an annual aggregate cap and a sunset. Emission-reducing equipment is made cheaper for the taxpayers who buy it.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Owens moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 481 out favorably.

measures.title: Public Land Use Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill changes provisions relating to public land use in the state.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires the Public Lands Policy Coordinating Office to recognize and promote the principles of multiple use and sustained yield on federal public lands within the state, and prohibits natural asset companies from purchasing or leasing state public lands. Multiple use and sustained yield is the stated standard, and the natural asset company ban forecloses the alternative of retiring land from use.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass H.B. 496 out favorably.

measures.title: School Chaplain Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill allows an LEA to permit a volunteer chaplain at a school.

issues.rationale: Introduced text permits an LEA to allow a volunteer chaplain in its schools, requires LEAs that do so to adopt policies and requirements for chaplains, and requires the State Board of Education to report to the Education Interim Committee. Opening the public school building to religious volunteers is the operative change.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Walter moved to pass H.B. 514 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Transportation, Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Balderree moved to pass H.B. 514 out favorably.

measures.title: Half-day Kindergarten Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions regarding half-day kindergarten to ensure that a student attending half-day kindergarten receives instruction in all of the kindergarten core competencies.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires half-day kindergarten instruction to meet minimum standards the State Board of Education sets, requires an LEA governing board to inform parents that the half-day option exists, and requires it to provide a designated half-day class once half-day enrollment reaches a threshold. A parent's option is disclosed and then guaranteed, which is the narrow parental-control end of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Clancy moved to pass H.B. 517 out favorably.

measures.title: Boards and Commissions Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies boards and commissions.

issues.rationale: First substitute text repeals roughly two dozen boards, commissions, task forces, and advisory councils outright and folds seven separate professional licensing boards into consolidated boards, along with repealing the COVID-19 Health and Economic Response Act chapter. It is a streamlining bill whose every clause removes or merges a standing body rather than creating one.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Brammer moved to pass H.B. 534 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McKell moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 534 out favorably.

measures.title: Licensing Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies licensing provisions related to abortion.

issues.rationale: Introduced text deletes the prohibition on the state issuing a license for an abortion clinic after May 2, 2023 and the related bar on a licensed abortion clinic performing abortions, and restores type I and type II abortion clinics to the licensed facility categories. Removing the licensing shutdown is what keeps clinic-based abortion legally available in the state.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Birkeland moved to pass H.B. 560 out favorably.

measures.title: Cannabis Business Tax Credit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts a cannabis business expenses income tax credit.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text enacts a nonrefundable income tax credit for business expenses related to selling medical cannabis in the state, and requires the Department of Agriculture and Food to report license applicants' tax identification numbers to the State Tax Commission. The credit exists to offset the federal deduction denial that makes cannabis retail uniquely expensive, which supports the legal medical market.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Bramble moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 71 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Watkins moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 71 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Law Enforcement Canine Pilot Program
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses grant funding for law enforcement canines.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates the Law Enforcement Canine Grant Program to fund the purchase, training, handling, and insuring of law enforcement canines, has the Department of Public Safety administer it with priority to small agencies, and adds a sunset. It is direct state funding of police capability.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Kennedy moved to pass S.B. 111 out favorably.

measures.title: Water Efficiency Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses programs for water efficiency.

issues.rationale: Fourth substitute text provides incentives for water efficient landscaping in new residential development, grants rulemaking authority to implement them, and sets a sunset date. Landscaping is where most residential water goes in this state, so incentivizing efficient installation at build time is a substantive conservation measure.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Stephanie Pitcher moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 118 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Bolinder moved to pass 4th Substitute S.B. 118 out favorably.

measures.title: Gestational Agreement Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to gestational agreements.

issues.rationale: First substitute text replaces the gestational agreement statute's references to a prospective gestational mother's husband with references to the mother's spouse, and removes the clause requiring that both spouses among the intended parents satisfy the married requirement in the gendered form. The statute stops assuming an opposite-sex marriage, which is a narrow recognition gain.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 126 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Dailey-Provost moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 126 out favorably.

measures.title: Criminal Monetary Threshold Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends the monetary threshold amounts required for certain offenses.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text doubles the monetary thresholds that set offense grades across the theft and fraud chapters, moving conduct down from felony to misdemeanor and from class A to class B, and the new sentencing section it enacts orders mental health or substance abuse screening on a second offense and supervised probation rather than prison on later ones. Both halves reduce severity.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Thatcher moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 128 out favorably.

measures.title: High-need School Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill provides for grants to local education agencies to employ additional educators in high-need schools.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires the State Board of Education to solicit proposals and award grants that an LEA must use to employ an additional first year educator in a high-need school, with matching funds, reporting, and a sunset. State money buys teaching positions in the schools that have the hardest time staffing them.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Riebe moved to pass S.B. 138 out favorably.

measures.title: Health Benefit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to health benefit plans and prescription drugs.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text defines a long-term drug as one an enrollee has been prescribed for at least one hundred eighty days and requires a health benefit plan to establish procedures, including notice, before requiring the enrollee to switch off that drug or when it leaves the formulary. Continuity of an established prescription is a narrow but real access protection.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Eliason moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 166 out favorably.

measures.title: Child Care Services Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts the Child Care Capacity Expansion Act.

issues.rationale: First substitute text enacts the Child Care Capacity Expansion Act, states its purpose, directs named state departments to collaborate on implementing it, and requires an annual report to legislative committees. The stated object is expanding capacity, but the mechanism is interagency coordination rather than money or slots, so it stays at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: House Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Ballard moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 176 out favorably.

measures.title: Property Tax Assessment Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to property tax assessment.

issues.rationale: Fifth substitute text gives a property owner additional remedies when valuation alone raises an assessment past a threshold with no significant change to the property, changes the burdens of proof at the county board of equalization and the State Tax Commission so the carrying party need not show substantial error, requires reporting when a county exceeds the threshold, and sets deferral and partial payment rules. The taxpayer's position in a valuation fight improves.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Christofferson moved to pass 3rd Substitute S.B. 182 out favorably.

measures.title: State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions regarding the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice.

issues.rationale: Fourth substitute text requires the Legislature to approve the sentencing and supervision length guidelines and the juvenile disposition guidelines developed by the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice, and adjusts the membership and duties of that commission and the sentencing commission. Guideline-setting moves from an executive commission to legislative sign-off, which is an institutional power shift.

measures.title: Optometrist Practice Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill allows an optometrist to perform certain laser procedures.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates a certification allowing an optometrist to perform specified laser procedures after required training, imposes reporting and standards on certified optometrists, requires the Office of Professional Licensure Review to recommend whether the practice should continue based on outcome data, and sets a sunset. A licensure barrier to performing a procedure is lowered under review conditions.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Balderree moved to pass S.B. 210 out favorably.

measures.title: Generational Water Infrastructure Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the development of water resources.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates the Water District Water Development Council under the Interlocal Cooperation Act with powers, duties, reporting, and consultation requirements, addresses expenditures from the Water Infrastructure Restricted Account, and creates the Utah water agent to negotiate for new water supply with a sunset. The bill builds standing capacity to develop and import water supply.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Scott D. Sandall moved to pass S.B. 211 out favorably.

measures.title: Medical Cannabis Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to medical cannabis.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text widens the address types medical cannabis may be delivered to, permits targeted marketing by pharmacies, processors, and clinics, lets additional medical providers recommend to the Compassionate Use Board, eases felony-related license bars, strengthens public employee protections for medical cannabis use, and gives a public employee a Labor Commission complaint route. The advertising limits it keeps are guardrails on a net expansion.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Watkins moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 233 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Property Tax Income Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions of the Property Tax Act.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text aligns the maximum annual renter's credit with the maximum allowed for the homeowner's credit, raising the ceiling on relief a qualifying renter can receive. It is one number, but unlike the two-way relief packages this wave refused, nothing in the bill withdraws relief from anyone.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Bramble moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 250 out favorably.

measures.title: Farming Equipment Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates a new chapter in Title 70, Commerce and Trade, which establishes the right to repair agricultural equipment.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires a manufacturer of agricultural equipment to give the owner or an unaffiliated repair provider access to the data, software, software updates, and parts needed to repair the equipment, and exempts the manufacturer from liability for repairs done by others. A farmer's ability to fix their own equipment is the whole point of the bill.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Kwan moved to pass S.B. 269 out favorably.

measures.title: Medical Preauthorization Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts provisions related to authorization requests.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates deadlines by which a managed care organization must respond to specified authorization requests and adds a reporting requirement. A hard clock on preauthorization decides whether covered care actually reaches the patient in time, which is why this outranks the disclosure-only preauthorization bills.
